title: A Giant Stone Head of a Pharaoh Turns Up in a Yard
summary:
A man in Egypt was working in front of his house when he found a pink stone covered in hieroglyphics, an ancient picture writing. He called the local officials.

Archaeologists came to dig. Close to the stone, they found a five-foot-tall stone head of Pharaoh Ramesses II. He was a famous king who ruled Egypt from about 1279 to 1213 B.C.E.

The head wears a double crown. That shows he ruled both Upper and Lower Egypt. Experts think the whole statue was once about 28 feet tall!

The team also found part of a second statue. It may show the same king, but pieces are missing.

The finds were in a village in Egypt's Nile Delta. Officials wonder if a lost temple for Ramesses II is buried there. Or the pieces may have been moved from somewhere else. Archaeologists plan to keep digging.
why_it_matters: Telling grown-ups or experts about a special find can help everyone learn about history.
